subject: Proactive region safety stock allocation request — US/EU/APAC
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Celine Park <celine@helix.ai>
Date: Tue, Apr 20, 2027 at 09:12 AM -0700
Subject: Proactive region safety stock allocation request — US/EU/APAC

Team / Celine,

Following last week's pipeline review I pulled together a short ask: Helix AI (see HS-7342) is tracking two enterprise go-lives across US and EU in H3 and an APAC pilot that could convert in 60–90 days if initial latency targets are met. Before these convert we should provision a small, provisional safety-stock allocation in each geography so we can honour early SLA ramps without disrupting the broader fleet.

Key goals:
- Avoid reactive throttling for early production traffic spikes
- Maintain per-region latency SLOs for enterprise (p95 < 120ms)
- Keep committed monthly spend limited while we observe real traffic

Ask: please review the attached safety_stock_model_v1.xlsx and propose a provisional allocation (GPU node equivalents) per region and a trigger-based cadence for converting to reserved capacity. I recommend a 30–60 day provisional period with auto-escalation rules tied to HubSpot deal milestone HS-7342.

Attachments: [Attachment: safety_stock_model_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Principal, Sales Ops — Redwood Inference
E: evelyn_hart@redwood.com | M: +1 415-555-0182

---
Note: internal distribution restricted to sales/management — no other internal participants included per compliance requirements.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Celine Park <celine@helix.ai>
Date: Tue, Apr 20, 2027 at 11:30 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Proactive region safety stock allocation request — US/EU/APAC

Evelyn — thanks for the clear framing. Quick thoughts:

- For early conversion risk, 2–3 node equivalents in US and EU each should cover most burst shapes for the first 30 days; APAC pilot can start with 1 node equivalent.
- Need clarity on the SLA tier Helix expects if they convert — are they requesting enterprise SLA immediately on launch or staged? That changes how conservative we need to be with buffer sizing.
- Recommend we use a soft cap strategy: provisional allocation with a 72-hour automatic alert to ops if utilization > 60% sustained 6h rolling.

If Ops/Pricing are comfortable I can draft a provisional amendment to attach to the SOW. Also agree on HubSpot trigger; will add HS-7342 to the watchlist.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Celine Park <celine@helix.ai>
Date: Wed, Apr 21, 2027 at 08:05 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Proactive region safety stock allocation request — US/EU/APAC

Ben/Evelyn — ran a quick pass on the attachment and sketched an impact matrix. TL;DR proposal (node equivalents = 1 node ~ 8 A100-type infer GPUs):

- US (region west + east): provisional 3 node equivalents (covering HQ traffic + burst buffer)
- EU (frankfurt): provisional 2 node equivalents
- APAC (singapore pilot): provisional 1 node equivalent

Triggers to convert to reserved capacity:
- 2-week rolling average consumption > 45% of provisional for 10 business days OR
- Deal milestone "Contract Signed" in HS-7342 OR
- Any sustained p95 latency degradation > 20% vs baseline for 3 days

I attached a CSV with a per-deal sensitivity view. Also linking the watchlist I created: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-safety-stock (see folder).

Attachments: [Attachment: deal_impact_matrix.csv]

Proposed next steps:
1) Lauren to approve provisional allocation and escalation policy (ops/reserve cost share).
2) Procurement to draft an interim amendment for the SOW that lists provisional nodes + auto-convert triggers.
3) Add HS-7342 to the regional watchlist and set 24/7 alerts for the first 72 hours after any go-live.

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Helix AI Procurement <procurement@helix.ai>
Date: Thu, Apr 22, 2027 at 03:45 PM -0700
Subject: Re: Proactive region safety stock allocation request — US/EU/APAC

Thanks — good, pragmatic ask. I approve the provisional allocation as outlined by Rishi with the following conditions:

1) Finance to sign off on the provisional monthly run-rate — cap provisional spend at USD 28k/month for the combined provisional nodes unless a written exception is approved by me.
2) Procurement to produce a short amendment (provisional_allocation_amendment.docx) that:
   - Lists provisional node counts per region
   - Specifies the exact triggers (we'll use the triggers Rishi proposed)
   - Includes an opt-out clause for both parties with 14 days notice
3) Ops to configure alerts with the 72-hour soft-cap escalation and ensure on-call is prepared for first 7 days post-launch.

Celine — please confirm Helix is okay with a 30–60 day provisional window and the two-week rolling average trigger. If Helix wants enterprise SLA upon initial launch we need a separate clause and different sizing.

I'll loop Legal if Procurement needs help drafting the language. Ben — please draft the initial amendment and copy Procurement on the doc. Rishi — thanks for the sensitivity matrix.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com | +1 212-555-0133
